papers.title: Effects of App-Based Mindfulness Training on Dental Patients' Anxiety Symptoms Prior to Undergoing Dental Surgery: Protocol for a Mixed Methods Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dental anxiety is associated with treatment avoidance, poor oral health-related quality of life, increased procedural complications, and poor postoperative recovery. Negative appraisals may exacerbate anxiety and increase emotional and physiological arousal. Mindfulness may improve attentional and emotional regulation, and reduce dental anxiety through improved self-regulation. OBJECTIVE: The present study aims to investigate the effects of an app-based mindfulness intervention among patients experiencing dental anxiety prior to undergoing surgery. METHODS: Using a mixed methods design consisting of a randomized controlled trial and semistructured interviews, 100 participants will be randomized to an app-based mindfulness training or a control condition. Data will be collected prior to the start of the intervention (T0), postintervention, but presurgery (T1), and postsurgery (T2). Our primary outcome is dental anxiety; secondary outcomes include general anxiety, perceived stress, positive and negative affect, mindfulness, and postoperative pain. Analyses of covariance, mixed analyses of variance, and independent-samples 1-tailed  RESULTS: Recruitment began in April 2026, and the first screening was completed on April 6, 2026. To date, 19 participants have completed the study, and 4 interviews have been completed. Study completion is projected for August 2027, with publication of the findings anticipated in December 2027. The study has not received any funding. Relative to T0, we expect significantly greater improvements across our primary and secondary outcomes among intervention group participants compared with control group participants at postbaseline time points. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings may inform future efforts to implement cost-effective interventions in dental care settings to manage dental anxiety in order to reduce both stress- and anxiety-related burdens for patients and dentists.

papers.title: Foot pressure dynamics during Taijiquan standing meditation.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Taijiquan is a low-impact mind-body training practice integrating mindfulness, balance, and controlled movement. Among its foundational practices, standing meditation (Zhan Zhuang) serves as a precursor to dynamic forms, fostering balance, relaxation, and internal focus. While Taijiquan's benefits are well-documented, limited quantitative research has explored the foot pressure dynamics underpinning skill acquisition, particularly during standing meditation. This exploratory pilot study investigated whether frequency-domain plantar-force features could provide preliminary quantitative indicators associated with practitioner skill progression across beginner, intermediate, and advanced competency levels. METHODS: A pressure mat was used to analyze regional foot pressures variations in the time and frequency domain. Twenty-three participants, categorized into beginner, intermediate, and advanced levels, performed controlled standing stances under standardized conditions. The data were analyzed using conventional unsupervised cluster algorithms (k-means, hierarchical, DBSCAN), and an established statistical hypothesis-testing framework. RESULTS: Advanced practitioners demonstrated distinct low-frequency oscillatory patterns compared with beginners. Unsupervised clustering revealed preliminary group structure consistent with practitioner experience without using expert-defined labels. A composite Euclidean-distance metric showed exploratory separation between expert-defined beginner and non-beginner groups in both training and small validation datasets, although these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the exploratory pilot design, small sample size, class imbalance, and the possibility that clustering structure may reflect sample-specific geometry rather than a generalizable population signal. CONCLUSION: By introducing numeric metrics and leveraging non-invasive sensor technology, this study establishes a scalable framework for skill assessment in low-impact, balance-based meditative-aerobic training (LBMAT). These findings highlight the value of incorporating wearable technology into such practices to boost training effectiveness and reduce injury risk.

papers.title: Developing a yoga intervention for improving dyspnoea and quality of life in patients with lung cancer: a Delphi method study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Yoga has demonstrated benefits in alleviating cancer-related symptoms and improving quality of life. However, existing research is limited by methodological inconsistencies, including insufficient detail, unclear rationale, and variability in the interventions used. This study aimed to document consensus-based recommendations regarding the consistency of yoga interventions for reducing dyspnoea and improving quality of life in people with lung cancer. METHODS: A modified Delphi method was employed to reach a consensus among yoga professionals experienced in supporting people with respiratory diseases and/or cancer. Participants completed two rounds of online surveys. The second-round survey was developed based on the responses from the first round. The survey questions focused on the frequency and duration, approaches and techniques to include or avoid, training and experience for yoga professionals, and barriers and facilitators to practicing yoga in the clinic. RESULTS: Thirty-three yoga professionals participated, with 19 completing the first and 15 the second round. A consensus (≥ 75% agreement) emerged that participants should attend at least four yoga sessions per week for 7 weeks. The four fundamental components of yoga-postures, breathing regulation, relaxation, and meditation-were considered essential. Consensus was also reached on recommended approaches and techniques for these four components, but no consensus on those to avoid. Barriers and facilitators to implementing yoga were also identified. CONCLUSION: The Delphi process has reached a consensus which provides a framework for assessing gaps in previous studies. Future research should focus on these consensus findings by implementing clinical trials to evaluate the effectiveness of yoga-based interventions for dyspnoea in people with lung cancer.

papers.title: Efficacy of a nurse-facilitated mindfulness-based management program on severity of childhood cancer symptom cluster-leukemia in adolescents with leukemia receiving chemotherapy: A multicenter randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: This study evaluated the efficacy of a mindfulness-based symptom cluster management program on CCSC-L severity and HRQoL. METHODS: A two-arm multicenter randomized controlled trial with repeated outcome measurements was conducted among 60 adolescents receiving induction chemotherapy at three tertiary hospitals in Thailand. Participants were stratified by hospital and randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either the program based on the Individual and Family Self-Management Theory plus usual care or usual care alone. The symptom cluster severity was assessed immediately after completion of the four-week structured intervention and at Weeks 4 and 8, and HRQoL at Week 12. Linear mixed-effects models and between-group comparisons were performed. RESULTS: Linear mixed-effects modeling demonstrated a significant group × time interaction for overall symptom cluster severity (p < .001). Compared with usual care, adolescents receiving the intervention demonstrated significantly lower overall symptom cluster severity at Week 4 (model-estimated mean difference = -0.90) and Week 8 (model-estimated mean difference = -1.63). Significant between-group differences favoring the intervention were observed across all five symptoms at both assessments (all unadjusted p ≤ .001). At Week 12, the complete-case analysis (intervention, n = 30; control, n = 28) showed higher overall HRQoL in the intervention group (mean difference = 11.59, 95% CI [8.56,14.62], unadjusted p < .001). CONCLUSIONS: The program reduced symptom cluster severity and improved HRQoL. These findings suggest that the intervention could be considered for integration into routine pediatric oncology nursing practice in similar clinical settings. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Thai Clinical Trials Registry (TCTR20250608004); prospectively registered on 8 June 2025, before the first participant was enrolled on 20 June 2025.

papers.title: Coping Strategies in Psychosis Spectrum Disorders: A Meta-Synthesis of Qualitative Evidence.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Psychotic spectrum disorders (PSDs), including schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder, significantly disrupt cognition, perception, and emotion, requiring individuals to develop diverse coping strategies for daily life. PURPOSE: This study aimed to systematically identify and synthesize coping mechanisms reported by individuals with PSDs, with particular attention to lived experiences and personal narratives. METHOD: A systematic literature search was conducted in accordance with the ENTREQ guidelines across PsycARTICLES, PubMed, and Embase. The included studies were appraised using the CASP checklist, and findings were synthesized employing a meta-ethnographic approach. To assess confidence in the synthesized themes, the CERQual framework was applied. RESULTS: A total of 24 relevant qualitative studies were included in the synthesis. Analysis revealed eight principal coping themes: (1) meaning-making and personal understanding of psychosis; (2) spiritual and religious coping; (3) social support and interpersonal connection; (4) active coping strategies, including behavioral regulation and mindfulness; (5) trauma-informed coping; (6) identity reconstruction and agency; (7) structure, routine, and goal-directed activity; and (8) cultural and contextual influences. Meaning-making and social support consistently correlated with psychological resilience and recovery. Spiritual coping demonstrated both adaptive and maladaptive patterns, varying with context. Structured daily routines and purposeful activity supported emotional stability and symptom management. CONCLUSION: Coping with psychosis is complex and multidimensional, encompassing more than symptom management. Effective coping involves identity reconstruction, meaning-making, and rebuilding social connections. These findings support the clinical integration of trauma-informed, culturally sensitive, and coping-oriented therapies in psychosis treatment. Further research should examine the evolving relationship between coping strategies and psychosocial outcomes to inform best practices in mental health care.

papers.title: Tired of Thinking? Think Again! A Longitudinal Experience-Sampling Study of Bidirectional Dynamics Between Rumination and Mental Fatigue in Athletes.
papers.abstract: Recovery days are intended to support psychological and physical recovery, yet repetitive sport-related thinking may interfere with this process. This four-week experience-sampling study examined the dynamic interplay between rumination and mental fatigue during rest days in competitive athletes, as well as the moderating roles of perfectionistic concerns and perfectionistic strivings. A total of 134 athletes completed repeated rest-day assessments of rumination and mental fatigue, with perfectionism measured at baseline using a sport-adapted version of the FMPS-Brief. Continuous-time structural equation modelling revealed significant bidirectional coupling between rumination and mental fatigue, supporting a self-reinforcing dynamic in which rumination fuels fatigue, and accumulated fatigue heightens the likelihood of further rumination, creating a 'vicious cycle'. The rumination → mental fatigue pathway was stronger than the reverse, underscoring the critical importance of mental rest and psychological recovery in sport. Perfectionistic concerns significantly moderated this association, suggesting that athletes high in evaluative self-criticism may be more vulnerable to the rumination-fatigue cycle, whereas perfectionistic strivings did not exert a moderating effect. These findings advance a process-oriented understanding of psychological recovery in athletes and may inform future research on how short-term rumination-fatigue dynamics contribute to longer-term maladaptive recovery patterns, including burnout risk. Interventions targeting repetitive negative thinking, such as mindfulness-, cognitive-behavioral-, or acceptance-based approaches, may help athletes preserve psychological recovery under performance demands.

papers.title: High Dispositional Mindfulness Is Associated With Lower Insomnia in College Students: A Retrospective Analysis.
papers.abstract: Mindfulness-based interventions have been shown to be effective for lowering insomnia symptoms in college students; however, it is not yet clear whether higher dispositional mindfulness is associated with lower insomnia symptoms. This information could help guide individual risk assessment for developing insomnia and future insomnia interventions. Thus, this secondary analysis was conducted to examine whether high dispositional mindfulness (corresponding to scores ≥ 3.71 on the MAAS) and low dispositional mindfulness (corresponding to scores < 3.71) are associated with severity of insomnia symptoms. Subjects (n = 2152) were selected from a sample of college students (n = 3160; 71.7% women; X¯ age = 22 ± 3.72 years). Subjects completed questionnaires assessing dispositional mindfulness, depression, anxiety, chronotype and insomnia symptoms. Linear regression models examined the association between dispositional mindfulness and insomnia symptoms and were used for moderation analyses to determine whether depression, anxiety, or chronotype moderated this relationship. High dispositional mindfulness was significantly associated with lower insomnia symptoms (Est = -4.166, SE = 0.225, p < 0.001). Neither depression, anxiety, nor chronotype moderated this relationship such that higher levels of any such variable were not associated with greater insomnia symptoms regardless of dispositional mindfulness. There was significantly lower anxiety and depression scores for those with high dispositional mindfulness (p < 0.05). These results suggest that those with high dispositional mindfulness may be less susceptible to insomnia. Findings support the plausibility of mindfulness training to ameliorate insomnia risk in young adults.

papers.title: An exploration of the roles of cognitive reactivity and ego depletion in the relationship between entrapment and suicidal ideation.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Entrapment is theorized as a key driver of suicidal ideation, yet the cognitive processes leading to entrapment, particularly the activating role of negative affect, and those through which entrapment translates into suicidal ideation are not well understood. Grounded in the Integrated Motivational-Volitional Model, this study used mediation analyses to examine cognitive reactivity in relation to suicidal ideation via entrapment, and ego depletion as a mediator of the entrapment-suicidal ideation link. DESIGN: A cross-sectional online survey was used to collect self-report data from participants recruited through opportunity sampling. METHODS: The sample consisted of 312 adults living in the United Kingdom. Data analyses were conducted on a subsample of participants who reported a lifetime history of suicidal ideation and/or suicide attempts (N = 269; M RESULTS: The relationship between cognitive reactivity and suicidal ideation was accounted for by entrapment; this indirect association was not moderated by trait mindfulness. Additionally, the entrapment-suicidal ideation relationship was partially accounted for by self-regulatory fatigue, but not by depletion sensitivity; this indirect effect remained significant after controlling for depression, but not anxiety diagnosis. CONCLUSIONS: The findings highlight cognitive reactivity as a cognitive vulnerability to suicidal ideation and underscore the value of understanding suicide risk through the lens of self-regulation. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and the observed associations should be interpreted as correlational in nature.
